prize_parts.citation: for discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and its active form that made incretin-based therapies for diabetes and obesity possible

statement.case_for: All six openings ranked B008 first, and I do not treat that unanimity as proof of merit. The merit rests on the chain itself. Holst established GLP-1 secretion and its insulinotropic action in humans. Drucker defined proglucagon-derived peptide biology and the tissue actions of GLP-1 and GLP-2. Mojsov identified the active truncated GLP-1(7-36) peptide. That chain led to a drug class that lowers glycaemia and body weight and has shown cardiovascular and renal benefit in large independent outcome trials over roughly two decades. The originality sits in physiology, the impact is clear and measurable, and the field is mature. As a neurologist I also note that the gut-brain axis and appetite circuits make this a physiology prize and not only a drug-development prize.
statement.case_against: The credited set has four names against a three-person limit, so any trio leaves out someone with a real claim. If the prize leans toward drug development, Knudsen is the obvious omission. If it leans toward physiology, the omission is Knudsen's industrial work, which made the therapies practical. Mojsov's priority for the active peptide is contested, and I cannot resolve it from the supplied material. Earlier peptide work outside the list, such as Habener's, is a further gap. There is also a risk that one achievement this large crowds out candidates such as CAR-T, SMA antisense therapy and HPV vaccination that are equally mature and cleanly attributed.

responses.point: She ranks B008 first but proposes Drucker, Holst and Knudsen, treating Mojsov's contribution as contested and giving weight to the pharmaceutical development of long-acting analogues.
responses.response: I take the Knudsen argument seriously, because liraglutide and semaglutide are why the physiology reached patients at scale. I still prefer Mojsov to Knudsen. The Nobel citation is for a discovery, and the identification of the active peptide is a discovery step that makes the physiology exploitable. Long-acting analogue design is excellent development work, but it is more an engineering of the discovery. I accept that the Mojsov attribution is the weakest point in my configuration. If the committee judges her priority too disputed to defend, the substitution of Knudsen is the credible alternative and I would not block it.

responses.point: He places optogenetics (B034) second, arguing that millisecond, cell-type-specific control of neural activity is among the most transformative tools in neuroscience, and he accepts Deisseroth, Nagel and Hegemann as a trio.
responses.response: I agree on scientific importance, since the tool has changed circuit neuroscience, including in my own field. I disagree that the attribution is manageable. Six credited names, with Bamberg, Boyden and Miesenböck outside any three-person set, make the choice arbitrary at the margin. The medical contribution is also still early, with retinal restoration the main clinical example. I would keep B034 as a serious future candidate but not as the preferred part this year.

responses.point: He ranks HPV virus-like particle vaccines (B031) fourth and argues that the 2008 prize recognised the HPV-cancer link and not the vaccine, with Zhou's death in 1999 making Lowy, Schiller and Frazer a workable trio.
responses.response: That distinction is correct, and it removes my main worry that B031 is already recognised. Registry data showing falling cervical cancer incidence give the case strong maturity. I still rank it below the leading candidates because the priority among VLP groups remains disputed, and I cannot verify from the supplied material how Zhou's contribution would be handled. I would move it up if the committee can resolve the priority question.

responses.point: He ranks the unfolded protein response (B024) fourth, with Walter and Mori as a clean two-person configuration, and treats CAR-T as a strong second.
responses.response: I agree that Walter and Mori form a clean pair. I treat B024 as basic biology whose disease relevance is still being established, and the PERK arm adds a possible attribution gap. On CAR-T I agree with his view, and it is my first alternative. Whether Rosenberg or a pair of June and Sadelain is more defensible is a judgement I would want the committee to settle.

uncertainties: Whether Mojsov or Knudsen, or both through a two-part split, best fits the three-person limit for B008.
How strongly to weigh a drug-development contribution against a physiological discovery within one achievement.
Whether CAR-T (B017) or SMA antisense therapy (B001) would be better as a second part if the committee prefers two achievements; the three-person total makes this hard.
Details of the Mojsov and Habener priority questions are not verifiable from the supplied files.
statement.conflict_note: My profile documents a roughly twenty-work co-authorship record with Thomas Perlmann, who is on this committee. None of the shortlisted candidates involves his work or mine, and none of the credited laureates is documented as a collaborator or Rockefeller colleague, so no specific conflict is apparent from the provided profile. B030 (deep brain stimulation) is in my clinical field but is not on the shortlist.
